Unit 1: Friends Around Us • Class 3 English (New NEP 2020)

Chapter 1: Fun with Friends

Playground Games, Sharing, Turn-Taking, New Friendships & Outdoor Sports

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • The joy of making new friends and playing traditional playground games.
  • Learning cooperation, empathy, and fair play in group games.
  • Vocabulary: playground equipment (swings, slide, see-saw) and action verbs.
  • Simple present tense sentences describing everyday play habits.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What games do the children play in the park in 'Fun with Friends'? Why is taking turns important when playing on playground swings? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. In the park, the children play games like hide-and-seek, tag, sliding down the slide, and swinging on swings.
2. Importance of taking turns: Taking turns ensures that every child gets a fair chance to play without arguments. It shows kindness, patience, and keeps the playground safe and friendly for everyone.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct mention of games played in the park 1.5 M
Moral explanation of fairness and safety in taking turns 1.5 M
Q2 Fill in the blanks with suitable action verbs: (run, swing, jump, laugh). (a) Children love to ___ on the swings. (b) We ___ across the grass during tag. (c) The friends ___ happily when hearing a funny riddle. Vocabulary & Word Power • Action Words 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answers:
• (a) Children love to swing on the swings.
• (b) We run across the grass during tag.
• (c) The friends laugh happily when hearing a funny riddle.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct verb for (a) swing 1.0 M
Correct verb for (b) run 1.0 M
Correct verb for (c) laugh 1.0 M
Q3 Write three short sentences about your best friend in school. Mention their name, what you like to share, and your favourite game together. Writing Prompts • My Best Friend 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Model Sentences:
1. My best friend's name is Aarav, and we sit together in Class 3.
2. We always share our lunch tiffins and colour pencils during art class.
3. Our favourite game to play during recess is badminton.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct grammar and spelling 1.5 M
All three specified details included 1.5 M
Q4 Look at the picture in Chapter 1 showing children playing near a pond:
(a) How many ducklings and chicks can you spot in the pond picture?
(b) Match each animal with its young one: Dog, Cat, Duck, Hen.
(c) What are the children doing to show friendship with animals? Picture Reading • Animals & Birds 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Step-by-Step Picture Reading & Vocabulary:
(a) Animal Count:
• In the picture, there are 3 yellow ducklings swimming behind mother duck and 4 little chicks pecking near the grass.

(b) Matching Animals with Young Ones:
• Dog $\rightarrow$ Puppy
• Cat $\rightarrow$ Kitten
• Duck $\rightarrow$ Duckling
• Hen $\rightarrow$ Chick.

(c) Showing Friendship:
• The children are feeding grain gently, smiling, and petting the animals without frightening or chasing them.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct picture identification of ducklings and chicks 1.0 M
Accurate matching of all 4 animal-offspring pairs 1.0 M
Thoughtful description of gentle friendship with animals 1.0 M
Q5 In the poem 'Colours':
(a) What color is the sky on a bright sunny day, and what color are the clouds when it rains?
(b) Name three green things mentioned or seen in nature.
(c) Write two pairs of rhyming words from the poem. Poem Comprehension • 'Colours' 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Step-by-Step Analysis:
(a) Colors of Sky and Clouds:
• On a sunny day, the sky is bright blue.
• When it rains, the clouds are dark grey (or black).

(b) Three Green Things:
• 1. Grass
• 2. Leaves on trees
• 3. Parrots.

(c) Rhyming Pairs:
• Bright — White
• Seen — Green.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct colors of sky (blue) and rain clouds (grey/black) 1.0 M
Three valid natural green items listed 1.0 M
Two correct rhyming pairs identified 1.0 M
Q6 Find and unjumble the color names hidden in these jumbled letters:
(a) L E Y W O L
(b) P L P E U R
(c) R N A O E G
(d) N K I P Word Search • Hidden Color Words 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Unjumbled Color Words:
• (a) L E Y W O L $\rightarrow$ YELLOW
• (b) P L P E U R $\rightarrow$ PURPLE
• (c) R N A O E G $\rightarrow$ ORANGE
• (d) N K I P $\rightarrow$ PINK
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct unscrambling for (a) and (b) 2.0 M
Correct unscrambling for (c) and (d) 2.0 M
Q7 (a) Have you ever shared your toys or crayons with a friend? How did it make you feel?
(b) Write two sentences about your best friend. Critical Thinking • 'Think and Say' 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Model Expressive Answer:
(a) Sharing Experience:
• Yes, I shared my set of wax crayons with my classmate when she forgot hers at home. It made me feel very happy, kind, and proud because we were able to color our pictures together.

(b) Two Sentences on Best Friend:
• 1. My best friend is Aarav, and we sit together on the front bench every day in school.
• 2. He always shares his lunchbox with me and helps me during art class.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Authentic personal reflection on sharing and empathy 1.5 M
Two grammatically correct sentences about a friend 1.5 M
Q8 In 'Fun with Friends', describe what key lesson or character trait is highlighted when the central character faces a challenge. How does this connect to real-life friendship or cooperation? Reading is Fun • Direct Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Textual Comprehension & Analysis:
1. In the story/poem Fun with Friends, the central character demonstrates perseverance, kindness, and teamwork when confronting difficulties.
2. When individuals cooperate rather than act selfishly, problems are resolved much faster and everyone benefits.
3. Real-Life Connection: In our daily lives, sharing tasks with classmates or family members builds trust and mutual respect, just as seen in this lesson.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identification of central trait (cooperation/kindness) 1.5 M
Valid real-world connection to friendship/teamwork 1.5 M
Q9 From the lesson 'Fun with Friends', find:
(a) Two rhyming words or sound-alike pairs.
(b) Write the opposite (antonym) of: Kind, Fast, Heavy.
(c) Form a meaningful sentence using one of the new vocabulary words from this chapter. Word Building • Vocabulary & Phonics 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Vocabulary Solutions:
• (a) Rhyming pairs: Day - Play, Round - Sound.
• (b) Opposites:
- Kind → Cruel / Unkind
- Fast → Slow
- Heavy → Light.
• (c) Sample Sentence: The children showed great kindness by helping the injured bird.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct rhyming pairs 1.0 M
Accurate opposites for all 3 words 1.0 M
Grammatically correct sentence 1.0 M
Q10 Have you ever had an experience similar to the events described in 'Fun with Friends'? Share what you did, who was with you, and how you felt afterward. Talk Time • Oral Expression & Personal Reflection 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Model Personal Reflection:
• Experience: Yes, during our school sports day, our relay team was trailing behind. Just like the theme in Fun with Friends, we encouraged each other and stayed calm.
• Action: In the final lap, our teammate ran with full determination, and we secured second place.
• Feeling: I felt proud and joyful because supporting each other brought us closer together.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear narration of personal experience 1.5 M
Expression of feelings and thematic alignment 1.5 M
Q11 Punctuate and rewrite the following sentences correctly using capital letters, commas, and full stops:
(i) rohan priya and amit went to the park on sunday
(ii) what a beautiful flower said the little girl Grammar & Language Structure • Sentence Mechanics 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Punctuation & Capitalisation:
• (i) Rohan, Priya, and Amit went to the park on Sunday. (Capitalized names, comma between items, capital S for Sunday, full stop at end).
• (ii) "What a beautiful flower!" said the little girl. (Capital W, quotation marks for speech, exclamation mark).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Sentence (i) correctly punctuated 1.5 M
Sentence (ii) correctly punctuated 1.5 M
Q12 Write a short 4-sentence paragraph describing your favorite part of 'Fun with Friends'. Why was that particular moment memorable to you? Let's Write & Creative Expression • Paragraph 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Model Paragraph:
My favorite moment in Fun with Friends is when the characters unite to achieve their common goal. The vivid illustrations and dialogue make the scene feel truly alive. It taught me that small acts of courage can make a big difference. This chapter inspires me to be a thoughtful and supportive friend every day.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Relevant content reflecting chapter theme 1.5 M
Coherent 4-sentence structure and correct grammar 1.5 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Welcoming a New Student

Real-Life Context: On Monday, a new girl named Zoya joined Class 3. She sat alone during lunchtime looking shy and nervous.

Analytical Task: What two friendly actions can Rohit and his group take to help Zoya feel welcomed and happy in school?

1. Rohit can walk over with a warm smile and invite Zoya to sit with their group to share snacks.
2. They can show her around the classroom and playground and invite her to join their team in a friendly game of hide-and-seek.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M first empathetic welcoming action + 1.5M second inclusive play action.

Unit 1: Friends Around Us • Class 3 English (New NEP 2020)

Chapter 2: Badal and Moti

Loyalty, Care for Animals, Rural Life, Bravery & Rescuing a Pet Dog

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • The bond of affection between a village boy, Badal, and his faithful pet dog, Moti.
  • Animal intelligence, loyalty, and protective instincts toward human family members.
  • Sequencing story events: daily walks, warning bark, river crossing, and rescue.
  • Descriptive adjectives: brave, faithful, swift, muddy, rushing.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 Who was Moti, and how did he show his loyalty when Badal slipped near the muddy stream? Let us Think • Story Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Who was Moti: Moti was Badal's beloved pet dog who accompanied him everywhere across the village fields.
2. Act of Loyalty: When Badal slipped on the muddy bank and fell near the swollen stream, Moti immediately barked loudly to alert village elders and firmly gripped Badal's shirt collar with his teeth to prevent him from being swept into deeper water until help arrived.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate identification of Moti as Badal's dog 1.0 M
Detailed description of barking and holding collar to rescue 2.0 M
Q2 Give the antonym (opposite word) for: (a) Deep, (b) Faithful, (c) Brave. Use 'faithful' in a meaningful sentence. Vocabulary • Synonyms & Antonyms 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Antonyms:
• (a) Deep × Shallow
• (b) Faithful × Unfaithful / Disloyal
• (c) Brave × Cowardly / Timid.

Sentence: 'Moti was a faithful companion who protected the family every night.'
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct antonyms for all 3 words 1.5 M
Meaningful, grammatically correct sentence using faithful 1.5 M
Q3 What responsibilities do pet owners have toward their pets? Mention three important duties. Speaking & Listening • Pet Care 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Pet Care Duties:
1. Nutritious Food & Fresh Water: Providing clean drinking water and healthy meals daily.
2. Shelter & Cleanliness: Giving pets a warm, dry sleeping space and regular baths.
3. Healthcare & Exercise: Taking them to veterinary doctors for vaccinations and taking them for regular walks.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Mention of food and clean water 1.0 M
Mention of shelter and healthcare/veterinary visits 2.0 M
Q4 In the story 'Badal and Moti', action words change to show things that happened in the past by adding '-ed'.
Change the following present verbs to past tense:
(a) Bark $\rightarrow$ _____
(b) Jump $\rightarrow$ _____
(c) Pull $\rightarrow$ _____
(d) Play $\rightarrow$ _____ Grammar & Verbs • Past Tense with '-ed' 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Past Tense Forms:
• (a) Bark $\rightarrow$ Barked (e.g., Moti barked loudly to alert the villagers).
• (b) Jump $\rightarrow$ Jumped (e.g., Badal jumped across the stream).
• (c) Pull $\rightarrow$ Pulled (e.g., The boy pulled the stick).
• (d) Play $\rightarrow$ Played (e.g., Badal and Moti played in the mud).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct past tense for (a) and (b) 2.0 M
Correct past tense for (c) and (d) 2.0 M
Q5 State whether each statement from 'Badal and Moti' is True ('T') or False ('F'):
(a) Moti was a naughty little monkey.
(b) Badal slipped and fell into deep mud near the pond.
(c) Moti ran away and did not help Badal.
(d) Badal's mother thanked Moti and gave him bread and milk. True or False • Story Retention 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
True/False Evaluation:
• (a) False [F]: Moti was a faithful, brave pet dog, not a monkey.
• (b) True [T]: Badal slipped on the muddy bank and fell in.
• (c) False [F]: Moti barked loudly, caught Badal's shirt collar, and helped pull him out to safety.
• (d) True [T]: Badal's mother hugged Moti with tears of joy and fed him lovingly.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct evaluations for (a) and (b) 2.0 M
Correct evaluations for (c) and (d) 2.0 M
Q6 Imagine your pet puppy or kitten is lost in the colony.
(a) What three things would you do to find it?
(b) How should we treat stray animals in our neighborhood? Speaking & Dialogue • Pet Care 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Step-by-Step Guide:
(a) Finding a Lost Pet:
• 1. Call out its name loudly and check familiar spots like parks, porches, and under cars.
• 2. Ask neighborhood friends, guards, and local shopkeepers if they saw it passing by.
• 3. Put up posters with its photo and a parent's phone number.

(b) Treating Stray Animals:
• We should treat stray animals with kindness, never throw stones at them, and provide clean water in earthen bowls, especially during hot summers.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three sensible, proactive search actions 1.5 M
Empathetic, responsible approach to neighborhood animals 1.5 M
Q7 Write the opposites of the following words from the lesson:
(a) Deep
(b) Safe
(c) Fast
(d) Loud Vocabulary • Opposite Words 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Opposites (Antonyms):
• (a) Deep $\times$ Shallow
• (b) Safe $\times$ Dangerous / Unsafe
• (c) Fast $\times$ Slow
• (d) Loud $\times$ Quiet / Soft
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct antonyms for (a) and (b) 2.0 M
Correct antonyms for (c) and (d) 2.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Animal Empathy Case Study

Real-Life Context: While walking home from school, Rohan spotted a stray puppy shivering under a tree on a rainy afternoon.

Analytical Task: What safe, compassionate steps should Rohan take with the help of his parents to care for the puppy?

1. Rohan should gently shelter the puppy from the rain using a dry cloth or cardboard box without frightening it.
2. He should inform his parents to provide a warm bowl of milk or puppy food.
3. Together with his parents, he should contact an animal welfare shelter or vet to ensure the puppy receives healthcare and vaccination.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M immediate protective care + 1.5M parental/veterinary consultation.

Unit 1: Friends Around Us • Class 3 English (New NEP 2020)

Chapter 3: Best Friends

School Friendships, Mutual Support, Studying Together & Conflict Resolution

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Qualities of true friendship: kindness, honesty, mutual encouragement, and understanding.
  • How friends help each other during difficult lessons and creative activities.
  • Resolving petty disagreements through honest conversation rather than anger.
  • Grammar: using singular and plural nouns correctly.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What makes Pooja and Neha best friends in the story? How do they help each other when one finds arithmetic difficult? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Pooja and Neha are best friends because they share everything, listen respectfully to each other, and encourage one another in every school task.
2. When Neha finds arithmetic sums difficult, Pooja patiently sits beside her, explains the steps using counters, and celebrates when Neha gets the correct answer.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Characteristics of their friendship 1.5 M
Explanation of how arithmetic support is given 1.5 M
Q2 Write the plural forms for: (a) Friend, (b) Story, (c) Class, (d) Wish. Make one sentence using 'friends'. Grammar • Singular and Plural Nouns 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Plural Forms:
• (a) Friend → Friends
• (b) Story → Stories (ending in consonant + y changes to -ies)
• (c) Class → Classes (words ending in -ss take -es)
• (d) Wish → Wishes (words ending in -sh take -es).

Sentence: 'All my friends cheered when our class won the quiz competition.'
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct plural forms for all 4 nouns 2.0 M
Correct, meaningful sentence using friends 1.0 M
Q3 If two friends both want to use the same storybook during library period, what is the best way to resolve the problem peacefully? Conflict Resolution • Role Play 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Peaceful Solution:
1. They can sit together and read the storybook together, turning pages by turn.
2. Alternatively, they can agree that one friend reads it during the first half of the period, and the second friend reads it during the second half.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Collaborative reading suggestion 1.0 M
Fair time-sharing agreement 1.0 M
Q4 Fill in the blanks with the correct article 'a' or 'an':
(a) Circle saw ___ apple on the tree.
(b) Triangle drew ___ triangle with three sharp corners.
(c) Square made ___ orange box.
(d) They drew ___ umbrella to protect themselves from rain. Grammar • Articles 'a' and 'an' 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Articles Rules (Vowel sounds take 'an', consonant sounds take 'a'):
• (a) Circle saw an apple on the tree ('a' sound $\rightarrow$ vowel).
• (b) Triangle drew a triangle with three sharp corners ('t' sound $\rightarrow$ consonant).
• (c) Square made an orange box ('o' sound $\rightarrow$ vowel).
• (d) They drew an umbrella to protect themselves from rain ('u' sound $\rightarrow$ vowel).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct articles for (a) and (b) 2.0 M
Correct articles for (c) and (d) 2.0 M
Q5 In the story 'Best Friends', Circle, Square, and Triangle argued about who is the most important.
(a) What did Circle boast about?
(b) What did Triangle boast about?
(c) How did they realize that they are best friends when working together? Shape Characters • Descriptive Vocabulary 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Comprehension:
(a) Circle's Boast:
• Circle said, 'I am round like the sun and the moon! Without me, wheels cannot roll and carts cannot move!'

(b) Triangle's Boast:
• Triangle said, 'I have three pointed corners and three straight sides! I make rooftops, mountains, and ice-cream cones!'

(c) Working Together:
• When they combined on paper, Triangle made the roof, Square made the walls, and Circle made the clock and doorknob to draw a beautiful house. They realized teamwork makes the best pictures.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate statement of Circle's boast 1.0 M
Accurate statement of Triangle's boast 1.0 M
Moral lesson of collaborative drawing explained 1.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Class Project Teamwork

Real-Life Context: Simran and Kabir were paired to make a science chart on 'Save Trees'. Kabir was good at drawing, while Simran wrote neat slogans and captions.

Analytical Task: How does dividing roles based on individual strengths help team projects succeed?

1. By dividing work according to what each member does best, both partners enjoy their task and feel valued.
2. Kabir's creative drawings and Simran's clear slogans combine to make a high-quality chart finished on time with zero conflict.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M explanation of role delegation + 1.5M positive outcome of combined strengths.

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Pollinator Protection Campaign

Real-Life Context: Students in Class 3 notice that gardeners are spraying harsh chemical weedkillers near flowering marigold beds, causing bees and butterflies to disappear.

Analytical Task: Why are bees and butterflies essential for flowers and crops? What safe advice should students give the school gardener?

1. Bees and butterflies are pollinators: they carry pollen grains from flower to flower, which helps plants produce seeds, flowers, and fruits.
2. Students should advise the gardener to avoid toxic chemicals and use natural organic compost, weeding by hand to protect beneficial pollinators.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M ecological role of pollination + 1.5M eco-friendly alternative advice.

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights

Q1 What do the toys talk about when the children go to sleep in 'Talking Toys'? What complaint did the teddy bear have? Let us Think • Story Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. When children go to sleep, the toys talk about how they were treated during playtime, sharing stories of being hugged, driven, or tossed around.
2. The teddy bear complained that he had been left upside down under the sofa where dust gathered, rather than being placed neatly on his warm bed shelf.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of night-time toy conversations 1.5 M
Specific mention of teddy bear's complaint under sofa 1.5 M

✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answers:
• (a) The teddy bear was found under the bed.
• (b) The toy train runs on the track.
• (c) Keep your building blocks in the wooden box.

Toy Donation Drive

Chapter 6: Paper Boats

Rabindranath Tagore's Poem, Monsoon Puddles, Distant Lands & Innocent Dreams

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Appreciating Rabindranath Tagore's poetic masterpiece 'Paper Boats'.
  • Writing one's name and village on boats to send messages to distant lands.
  • Loading boats with Shiuli flowers blooming in the dawn.
  • Metaphor of white bulging clouds racing with the paper boats.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 In Rabindranath Tagore's poem 'Paper Boats': (a) What does the child write on the paper boats? (b) What flowers does the child load into the boats, and why? Let us Think • Poetry Analysis 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poetic Analysis:
• (a) Writing on boats: The child writes their name and the name of their village in big black letters, hoping someone in a strange distant land will find them and know who sent them.
• (b) Flower cargo: The child loads the boats with Shiuli blossoms gathered from the garden at dawn, hoping these blooms of the night will be safely ferried to land in the dark.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct name and village writing explanation 1.5 M
Correct identification of Shiuli flowers and dawn harvest 1.5 M
Q2 What does the child imagine about the clouds in the sky? How do the clouds relate to the paper boats? Poetic Devices • Metaphor & Imagery 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Imagery Explanation:
The child looks up and sees little white clouds with bulging sails floating in the blue sky. The child imagines that an unseen playmate in the sky sends these cloud-ships down through the air to race with their own paper boats floating down the stream.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate description of cloud playmates and air racing 2.0 M
Q3 What kind of paper is best suited for making paper boats, and what should students do with wet paper boats after playing in rainwater puddles? Hands-on Activity • Origami & Recycling 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Activity & Eco-Awareness:
1. Suitable Paper: Used drawing sheets or scrap newspaper that hold folds firmly.
2. Environmental Responsibility: Wet paper boats should never be left to clog drains or litter roads. Once play is over, the soggy paper should be collected and deposited in a recycling or compost bin.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identifies scrap/recycled paper 1.0 M
Emphasizes eco-cleanup and preventing clogged drains 1.0 M
Q4 In 'Paper Boats':
(a) What type of paper is best for making paper boats that do not sink quickly: thin tissue paper or thick glossy/waxed paper? Why?
(b) Write two things children write or draw on their paper boats before floating them in rain puddles. Craft & Science • Paper Boats & Floating 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Craft & Physics:
(a) Best Paper:
• Thick waxed or waterproof paper is best because it does not absorb water quickly. Thin tissue paper absorbs water immediately, turns soggy, and sinks.

(b) Writing on Paper Boats:
• Children write their own name and address/school, or draw a small flag or flower, hoping it sails safely to distant lands.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct paper choice with scientific reasoning (water absorption) 1.5 M
Two authentic details children write/draw on boats 1.5 M
Q5 Classify the following items into 'Will Float on Water' and 'Will Sink in Water':
Dry leaf, Iron nail, Plastic bottle cap, Pebble, Wooden pencil, Glass marble. Science Exploration • Sink or Float? 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Float or Sink Classification:
• Will Float on Water:
1. Dry leaf (Light, low density)
2. Plastic bottle cap
3. Wooden pencil (Wood floats)

• Will Sink in Water:
1. Iron nail (Heavy metal, high density)
2. Pebble (Dense stone)
3. Glass marble.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct floating items classified (3 items) 1.5 M
Correct sinking items classified (3 items) 1.5 M

(a) Sail $\rightarrow$ _____
(b) Sea $\rightarrow$ _____
(c) Cloud $\rightarrow$ _____ Rhyming Words • 'Boats Sail on the Rivers' 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Rhyming Pairs:
• (a) Sail $\rightarrow$ Gale / Mail / Tail
• (b) Sea $\rightarrow$ Tree / Free / Me
• (c) Cloud $\rightarrow$ Loud / Proud
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Valid rhyming words for all three prompts 3.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Cultural Heritage of Rabindranath Tagore

Real-Life Context: Rabindranath Tagore was a Nobel Prize-winning poet who wrote India's National Anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana', and founded Visva-Bharati University in Santiniketan.

Analytical Task: How does Tagore's poetry encourage young children to connect with nature, simple toys, and universal human brotherhood?

1. Tagore's poems celebrate simple natural wonders—rain streams, paper toys, flowers, and open skies—showing that immense happiness comes from imagination rather than expensive gadgets.
2. Sending paper boats to unknown children in faraway lands embodies his belief in universal love and peaceful connection among all human beings.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M connection with natural imagination + 1.5M theme of universal brotherhood.

Chapter 7: The Big Laddoo

Humour, Folk Tale, Cooperation, Problem Solving & Festival Celebrations

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Folk tale humour: making an enormous festive laddoo that cannot fit through the door.
  • Cooperative problem solving: how the entire community pitches in to share and celebrate.
  • Sequencing ingredients: chickpea flour (besan), ghee, sugar, cardamom, and dry fruits.
  • Understanding size adjectives: tiny, big, huge, gigantic, enormous.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why did the sweet-maker make such an enormous laddoo in 'The Big Laddoo'? What problem arose once the laddoo was prepared? Let us Think • Story Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Reason: The sweet-maker wanted to prepare a grand sweet for the village festival that everyone would remember and talk about with pride.
2. The Problem: The laddoo turned out so gigantic that it was wider than the sweet-shop door! It could not be carried out into the courtyard without breaking the doorway.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct festival celebration motive 1.5 M
Accurate identification of the door width predicament 1.5 M
Q2 How did the villagers solve the problem of the oversized laddoo without breaking down the shop door? Problem Solving • Community Action 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Solution:
Instead of forcing the giant laddoo through the doorway, the village elders suggested inviting everyone inside the spacious kitchen courtyard. The sweet-maker portioned the laddoo into hundreds of sweet bowls, sharing a portion with every child and family in the village.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clever resolution through on-site distribution and sharing 2.0 M
Q3 Arrange these size adjectives in order from smallest to biggest: (Huge, Tiny, Enormous, Small, Gigantic). Vocabulary • Degrees of Size 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Order from Smallest to Biggest:
1. Tiny
2. Small
3. Huge
4. Gigantic
5. Enormous
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct ascending arrangement of all 5 adjectives 2.0 M
Q4 In the story 'The Big Laddoo', Grandmother makes a special gigantic laddoo for the children:
(a) Arrange the cooking steps in correct chronological order (1 to 4):
• Shape into round balls using palms.
• Roast besan (gram flour) in pure ghee till golden brown.
• Cool slightly and mix in powdered sugar and cardamom.
• Garnish with chopped almonds and pistachios.
(b) Why did Grandmother make one huge laddoo instead of many small ones? Recipe Sequencing • The Big Laddoo 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Step-by-Step Cooking Sequence:
(a) Correct Order:
1. Roast besan in pure ghee till golden brown.
2. Cool slightly and mix in powdered sugar and cardamom.
3. Shape into round balls using palms.
4. Garnish with chopped almonds and pistachios.

(b) The Huge Laddoo:
• Grandmother wanted all the children to sit in a circle, break pieces from the same giant laddoo together, and learn the joy of sharing.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct chronological order (1 to 4) 2.0 M
Moral purpose of unity and sharing explained 1.0 M

• (c) Saucepan / Kettle.

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Community Festival Food Sharing

Real-Life Context: At a community Langar / Bhandara feast, volunteers cook sweet halwa for 400 people. Some children want to serve elderly visitors first.

Analytical Task: What core human values are practiced when people cook together and serve food respectfully to everyone regardless of background?

1. Equality & Humility: Serving everyone equally without discrimination teaches mutual respect.
2. Community Spirit & Compassion: Respecting elders and sharing resources selflessly ensures nobody in the community goes hungry.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M concept of equality and respect + 1.5M selfless service and community solidarity.

Chapter 8: Thank God!

Gratitude, Appreciation of Senses, Nature's Blessings & Daily Thanksgiving

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Gratitude for human senses: eyes to see, ears to hear, tongue to taste, hands to hold.
  • Appreciation for daily life necessities: clean water, nutritious food, shelter, and family love.
  • The psychological benefits of practicing thankfulness every morning and night.
  • Rhyming scheme and prayer-song cadence.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 List four things the poet is thankful for in the poem 'Thank God!'. Why is it important to count our blessings? Let us Think • Poem Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poem Analysis:
1. Four Blessings:
• The sweet world filled with singing birds
• Nutritious food to eat each day
• Loving parents, family, and good teachers
• Healthy eyes, ears, and hands to learn and play.
2. Importance: Counting blessings cultivates positivity, contentment, and empathy, preventing complaints about trivial troubles.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Four correct blessings mentioned from poem 2.0 M
Moral reflection on contentment and thankfulness 1.0 M
Q2 Match each sense organ with its primary function: (1) Eyes, (2) Ears, (3) Tongue, (4) Skin. Actions: (Feel texture, Hear melodies, Taste flavours, See colours). Vocabulary • Sense Organs & Verbs 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Matching:
• 1. Eyes → See colours
• 2. Ears → Hear melodies
• 3. Tongue → Taste flavours
• 4. Skin → Feel texture.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct matching for all 4 pairs 2.0 M
Q3 Write three things you are grateful for today in your personal life. Personal Writing • Gratitude Journal 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Sample Gratitude Journal Entry:
1. I am grateful for the delicious breakfast my mother made for me this morning.
2. I am grateful for my school teacher who taught us an exciting story in English class.
3. I am grateful for my friends who played football with me in the afternoon.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

Grammar, spelling, and sentence construction 1.5 M
Q4 In 'Thank God!':
(a) What prayer or expression of gratitude did the family recite before eating their meals?
(b) Name the three main meals eaten in a day from morning to night.
(c) Why should we not waste food on our plates? Gratitude & Manners • Thank God! 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Step-by-Step Response:
(a) Gratitude Prayer:
• The family folded hands and thanked God, the farmers who grew the crop, and mother who cooked it with love.

(b) Three Main Meals:
• 1. Morning: Breakfast
• 2. Afternoon: Lunch
• 3. Night: Dinner / Supper.

(c) Preventing Food Waste:
• Farmers work hard in fields under the scorching sun for months to grow grain, and millions of poor people sleep hungry. Wasting food disrespects human labor and nature.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of mealtime thanksgiving 1.0 M
Three meals correctly named in chronological sequence 1.0 M
Empathetic, mature reason for not wasting food 1.0 M

Polite Table Phrases:

Gratitude & Well-Being Habit

Real-Life Context: Studies show that children who write down three positive events before going to bed sleep better and feel more confident in school.

Analytical Task: How can maintaining a classroom 'Gratitude Tree' on a soft board improve classroom harmony?

1. A Gratitude Tree allows students to pin sticky leaf notes expressing appreciation when a classmate shares an eraser or helps with schoolwork.
2. It builds mutual kindness, reduces bullying, and makes every child feel recognized and valued in class.

Chapter 9: Madhu's Wish

Wishes, Magic Paintbrush, Helping Others, Selflessness & Moral Values

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • The classic moral theme: selfish desires vs using gifts for the public good.
  • Madhu's wish for a magic paintbrush that paints objects into reality.
  • Painting food and plows for poor villagers rather than gold for greedy kings.
  • Using modal verbs: 'could', 'would', 'should' in wishing sentences.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What special power did Madhu's paintbrush have? What did Madhu choose to paint with it? Let us Think • Story Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Special Power: Whatever Madhu painted with his magic paintbrush came alive into real existence.
2. Madhu's Choice: Instead of painting gold or jewels for himself, Madhu painted water buffaloes to plow dry fields, bags of grain for hungry families, and warm blankets for shivering elders.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct explanation of the paintbrush's magical power 1.5 M
Mention of buffaloes, grain, and blankets for villagers 1.5 M
Q2 When a greedy moneylender demanded that Madhu paint a mountain of gold, what did Madhu do? What moral lesson does this teach? Moral Reasoning • Character Analysis 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Moral Analysis:
1. Madhu's Action: Madhu refused to help the greedy man become richer. When forced, he painted a deep ocean with a golden island far away and painted a boat that sailed away, stranding the greedy man without causing harm.
2. Moral Lesson: Greed leads to downfall; talents should never be surrendered to injustice or selfish exploitation.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of Madhu's clever resistance to greed 1.5 M
Clear formulation of the moral lesson 1.5 M
Q3 Complete the conditional wishing sentences: (a) If I had a magic paintbrush, I would paint ___. (b) If I could fly like a bird, I would visit ___. Grammar • Sentence Formulation 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Model Completions:
• (a) If I had a magic paintbrush, I would paint fresh green forests and clean rivers for endangered animals.
• (b) If I could fly like a bird, I would visit the snowy peaks of the Himalayan mountains.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Grammatically correct conditional sentence for (a) 1.0 M
Grammatically correct conditional sentence for (b) 1.0 M
Q4 In the story 'Madhu's Wish':
(a) What magical creature appeared in Madhu's dream, and what gift was she offered?
(b) What were the three wishes Madhu thought about?
(c) What did Madhu finally wish for that brought real happiness? Story Comprehension • Madhu's Wish 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Breakdown:
(a) Magical Creature:
• A glowing fairy with shimmering silver wings appeared and offered Madhu three magical wishes.

(b) Three Wishes Considered:
• 1. An endless supply of chocolates and ice cream.
• 2. A mountain of beautiful toys and dollhouses.
• 3. Wings to fly anywhere in the sky.

(c) Final Wise Wish:
• Madhu realized that toys get old and sweets finish quickly, so she wished for good health, wisdom, and happiness for her family and friends.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct fairy character identified 1.0 M
Three imaginative wishes listed 1.0 M
Selfless final wish and moral explained 1.0 M
Q5 If a magical fairy granted you three wishes today, what would you ask for and why? Write three bullet points. Creative Writing • If I had Three Wishes 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Model 3-Wish Reflection:
• Wish 1: A magical tree that grows fresh fruits for poor and hungry children all over the city.
• Wish 2: A pair of magical goggles that helps me see and clean up all plastic litter on beaches and forests.
• Wish 3: That my grandparents never fall sick and live happily for 100 years.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three original, empathetic, and imaginative wishes written 3.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Real-Life Magic of Volunteering

Real-Life Context: During winter, a group of schoolchildren collected old woollen sweaters, cleaned them, and distributed them to homeless pavement dwellers.

Analytical Task: How does this real-life act carry the exact same 'magic' as Madhu's paintbrush in the folk tale?

1. In real life, humans do not have magical paintbrushes, but our compassion, hands, and collective effort create real miracles.
2. By giving warm clothes to shivering people, the students transformed cold despair into warmth and safety, proving that empathy is the truest magic in the world.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M connecting metaphorical magic with human kindness + 1.5M real-world social impact.

Unit 4: Exploring the World • Class 3 English (New NEP 2020)

Chapter 10: Night

Night Sky, Moon, Stars, Nocturnal Animals, Quiet Slumber & Peaceful Rest

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Natural phenomena of night: sunset, darkness, twinkling stars, and changing phases of the moon.
  • Nocturnal creatures: owls, fireflies, and bats that become active after sunset.
  • The value of peaceful rest and sleep for physical growth and mental health.
  • Contrasting day activities (loud, bright, busy) with night tranquility (quiet, calm, dark).
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What changes take place in nature when day turns into night? Name two animals that stay awake during the night. Let us Think • Poem Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Changes in Nature: The sun sets beneath the horizon, darkness spreads over the sky, the air cools down, flowers close their petals, and stars begin to twinkle alongside the glowing moon.
2. Nocturnal Animals: Owls and bats (or fireflies) stay awake and active during the night.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Detailed description of evening and nightfall changes 1.5 M
Two correct nocturnal animals named 1.5 M
Q2 Give the opposites for: (a) Day, (b) Dark, (c) Sleep, (d) Loud. Vocabulary • Day vs Night Antonyms 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Antonyms:
• (a) Day × Night
• (b) Dark × Bright / Light
• (c) Sleep × Wake
• (d) Loud × Quiet / Silent.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct antonyms for all 4 words (0.5M each) 2.0 M
Q3 Why is getting 8 to 9 hours of uninterrupted sleep every night important for growing children in Class 3? Health & Well-Being • Sleeping Habits 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Importance of Sleep:
1. Physical Growth: Growth hormones are released primarily during deep sleep, helping bones and muscles develop.
2. Brain Memory: Sleep allows the brain to organize lessons learned during the day, improving memory, alertness, and mood in school.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Physical growth explanation 1.5 M
Brain restoration and memory consolidation 1.5 M
Q4 In the poem 'Night':
(a) What heavenly body lights up the earth when the sun goes to rest?
(b) What do the stars in the dark sky look like according to the poet?
(c) Which animals become active at night (nocturnal creatures)? Poem Comprehension • 'Night' 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poem Analysis:
(a) Night Light:
• The Moon lights up the earth with its cool, gentle silver rays.

(b) Stars Description:
• The poet compares the sparkling stars to glittering diamonds or tiny lamps glowing across the dark velvet sky.

(c) Nocturnal Animals:
• Owls, bats, fireflies, and moths become active at night.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct identification of the Moon 1.0 M
Poetic imagery of stars explained 1.0 M
Two or more nocturnal creatures named 1.0 M
Q5 Why does the earth have day and night? Explain in two simple sentences for a Class 3 student. Science Connection • Day vs Night 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Scientific Explanation:
1. The Earth spins continuously like a top around its own axis once every 24 hours.
2. The side facing the Sun receives light and has Day, while the side turned away from the Sun is in darkness and has Night.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Mention of Earth's rotation (spinning) 1.0 M
Clear relationship between facing the sun and day/night 1.0 M
Q6 Write the opposites of these words from the poem:
(a) Dark $\times$ _____
(b) Sleep $\times$ _____
(c) Gentle $\times$ _____
(d) Silence $\times$ _____ Opposites • Night and Day Vocabulary 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Antonyms:
• (a) Dark $\times$ Light / Bright
• (b) Sleep $\times$ Wake
• (c) Gentle $\times$ Harsh / Rough
• (d) Silence $\times$ Noise
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct opposites for all 4 words 4.0 M
Q7 Write two healthy habits you should follow every night before going to bed. Bedtime Routine • Personal Expression 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Healthy Bedtime Habits:
1. Brush your teeth properly with fluoride toothpaste to protect them from cavities overnight.

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Light Pollution Awareness

Real-Life Context: In large cities with bright neon signs and streetlights, children rarely see more than a handful of stars at night, whereas in village skies thousands of stars are clearly visible.

Analytical Task: What is 'light pollution', and how does excessive artificial light affect both stargazers and nocturnal wildlife?

1. Light pollution is the excessive, misdirected artificial illumination of the night sky by human cities.
2. It hides the beauty of constellations from stargazers and disorients nocturnal creatures like migrating birds, sea turtles, and night insects who rely on darkness for navigation.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M definition of light pollution + 1.5M ecological impact on navigation.

Chapter 11: Chanda Mama Counts the Stars

Moon Lore, Counting Stars, Bundles of Tens & Astronomical Curiosity

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Traditional Indian folklore: affectionate representation of the Moon as 'Chanda Mama'.
  • Counting enormous numbers by grouping: Chanda Mama grouping stars into packets of 10 and 100.
  • Connection between language arts and foundational mathematical grouping.
  • Astronomical wonder: understanding that stars are distant burning suns.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why was Chanda Mama having trouble counting the stars in the sky? What clever system of cards did he invent to keep count? Let us Think • Story Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. The Trouble: There were so many twinkling stars appearing and disappearing across the vast sky that Chanda Mama lost count whenever a star moved.
2. The Card System:
• For every single star, he put a [1] card in his pocket.
• When he collected ten [1] cards, he exchanged them for one [10] card.
• When he collected ten [10] cards, he exchanged them for one big [100] card.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of difficulty with infinite twinkling stars 1.0 M
Detailed breakdown of the base-10 card exchange system 2.0 M
Q2 If Chanda Mama has these cards in his pocket, what is the total number of stars counted? (a) Two [100] cards, three [10] cards, and four [1] cards. (b) Three [100] cards and eight [1] cards. Mathematical Integration • Cards to Numbers 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Calculations:
• (a) (2 × 100) + (3 × 10) + (4 × 1) = 200 + 30 + 4 = 234 stars.
• (b) (3 × 100) + (0 × 10) + (8 × 1) = 300 + 0 + 8 = 308 stars.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct calculation for (a) 234 1.0 M
Correct calculation for (b) 308 (handling zero tens) 1.0 M
Q3 Write a short two-line greeting that a child on Earth would say to the Moon through their bedroom window. Creative Dialogue Writing 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Model Greeting:
'Namaste, Chanda Mama! Thank you for lighting up our dark night with your gentle, silver glow.'
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Appropriate child-friendly tone and expression 1.0 M
Correct punctuation and poetic quality 1.0 M
Q4 In the delightful tale 'Chanda Mama Counts the Stars':
(a) Why did Chanda Mama want to count the stars in the sky?
(b) Why did he find it so difficult to count them all?
(c) What clever advice did Mother Earth give to Chanda Mama? Story Comprehension • Chanda Mama 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Breakdown:
(a) Counting Purpose:
• Chanda Mama wanted to know exactly how many little sparkling star-children he had in his sky family.

(b) The Difficulty:
• The stars kept twinkling, blinking, moving, and hiding behind passing clouds, which caused Chanda Mama to lose count again and again.

(c) Mother Earth's Advice:
• Mother Earth smiled and said, 'Do not worry about counting them all! Simply shine your silver light on them, and they will twinkle back with love.'
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct motive of counting star family 1.0 M
Clear reason why counting stars is impossible (twinkling/clouds) 1.0 M
Wise advice of Mother Earth explained 1.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Constellations & Pattern Recognition

Real-Life Context: Ancient astronomers grouped bright stars into pictures of hunters, bears, and queens called constellations (like Saptarishi / Ursa Major).

Analytical Task: How did grouping stars into recognizable patterns help ancient travelers and sailors navigate across open oceans at night?

1. In ancient times before GPS or compasses, stars provided fixed landmarks in the sky.
2. By locating the Saptarishi constellation and following its pointer stars to the North Star (Dhruva Tara), sailors could always identify true North and steer ships safely without getting lost.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M purpose of constellations as sky landmarks + 1.5M locating the North Star for navigation.

Chapter 12: Chandrayaan

India's Moon Mission, Vikram Lander, Pragyan Rover, ISRO Pride & Science

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Celebrating India's historic achievement: Chandrayaan-3 landing on the Moon's South Pole.
  • Key spacecraft components: propulsion module, Vikram lander, and Pragyan rover.
  • The dedication of ISRO scientists, teamwork, and scientific perseverance.
  • National pride and inspiring young students to pursue space science and STEM.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What was the historic achievement of India's Chandrayaan-3 mission? What are the names of the lander and the rover? Let us Think • Science Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Historic Achievement: On 23 August 2023, India became the first country in the world to successfully land a spacecraft near the challenging South Pole of the Moon, and the fourth country to achieve a soft landing on the lunar surface.
2. Components:
• The lander was named Vikram (in honour of Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, father of the Indian space programme).
• The six-wheeled robotic rover was named Pragyan (which means 'wisdom' in Sanskrit).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct statement of first country at Moon's South Pole 1.5 M
Correct naming of Vikram lander and Pragyan rover 1.5 M
Q2 Explain in simple words what a 'Rover' does on the Moon's surface. What was Pragyan looking for? Scientific Vocabulary • Space Technology 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Explanation:
• A rover is a small robotic vehicle equipped with wheels, cameras, and scientific instruments that can drive over the rocky lunar soil.
• Pragyan's mission: Pragyan rolled down the ramp to analyse lunar soil and rocks, taking temperature measurements and confirming the presence of elements like sulphur, oxygen, iron, and traces of water ice beneath the lunar surface.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Definition of a lunar rover as a wheeled robotic explorer 1.5 M
Scientific investigation of soil, minerals, and water ice 1.5 M
Q3 Why is 23rd August celebrated every year as 'National Space Day' in India? National Pride & Career Inspiration 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Significance:
The Government of India declared 23rd August as National Space Day to commemorate the historic success of the Chandrayaan-3 soft landing on the Moon, honour the brilliant women and men scientists of ISRO, and inspire future generations of students to pursue careers in space research and engineering.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Commemoration of Chandrayaan-3 landing 1.0 M
Honouring ISRO scientists and inspiring youth 1.0 M
Q4 In Chapter 12 'Chandrayaan':
(a) What was the name of the historic mission launched by India to explore the Moon?
(b) What is the name of the Lander and the Rover that safely touched down on the Moon's South Pole?
(c) Which organization built and launched this spacecraft? Inspirational Reading • Chandrayaan Mission 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Chandrayaan Historical Facts:
(a) Mission Name:
• Chandrayaan-3.

(b) Lander and Rover Names:
• The Lander was named Vikram (honoring Dr. Vikram Sarabhai).
• The Rover was named Pragyan (meaning 'Wisdom').

(c) Space Agency:
• ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct mission name (Chandrayaan-3) 1.0 M
Correct lander (Vikram) and rover (Pragyan) names 1.0 M

Q5 Match each space term with its meaning:

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Scientific Resilience & Failure to Success

Real-Life Context: In 2019, Chandrayaan-2's lander lost communication just 2 km above the lunar surface and crashed. Instead of giving up, ISRO scientists analyzed every error and redesigned Chandrayaan-3 with stronger legs and better sensors.

Analytical Task: What life lesson does ISRO's journey from Chandrayaan-2 to Chandrayaan-3 teach school students about dealing with failure in examinations and life?

1. Failure is not the end of the road; it is a powerful stepping stone to future success if one learns honestly from mistakes.
2. By calmly analyzing what went wrong, correcting their methods, and working together as a determined team, ISRO proved that perseverance and hard work always turn failure into historic victory.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M learning from mistakes and perseverance + 1.5M inspiring message on overcoming setbacks.

Unit 1: Morning & Nature • Class 3 English (Classic CBSE)

Unit 1: Good Morning & The Magic Garden

Poem by Fannie R. Buchanan & Story of School Children Loving and Watering Garden Flowers

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'Good Morning': Wishing the sky, sun, little winds, grass, and bees good morning.
  • Story 'The Magic Garden': Roses, sunflowers, marigolds, and poppies in the school garden.
  • Why flowers love little children: children bring water cans, dig the ground nicely, and bring breadcrumbs for birds.
  • Fairies in the garden: singing sweet songs that only children can hear.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why is the child in the poem 'Good Morning' happy? Why did the flowers love the little school children in 'The Magic Garden'? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Child's Happiness: The child is happy because night has passed, morning has arrived, and the child is wide awake to run out and play with the sun, sky, wind, birds, and bees.
2. Why Flowers Loved Children: The flowers loved the little children because they brought their watering cans to pour cool water on their thirsty roots and dug the soil around the plants tenderly.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of child's joy at morning waking 1.5 M
Two reasons why flowers loved children (watering and caring) 1.5 M

Q7 Explain how to make a dried flower scrapbook as described in the textbook activity. Team Time • Flower Scrapbook Activity 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Step-by-Step Dried Flower Scrapbook Guide:
1. Collection: Collect fallen petals and leaves from the garden (never pluck live flowers needlessly).
2. Pressing: Place the flowers carefully between the sheets of an old newspaper or heavy telephone directory.
3. Drying: Place heavy books on top and leave undisturbed for 4 to 5 days until all moisture is absorbed.
4. Mounting: Gently paste the dried flowers in a scrapbook using a dab of glue, and write their English and local names underneath.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

School Herbal Garden Care

Real-Life Context: Class 3 students decided to maintain a small botanical patch in school with tulsi, mint, aloe vera, and marigolds.

Analytical Task: What daily care routine should students establish to ensure their garden stays healthy throughout the year?

1. Water the plants gently in the early morning or evening so water does not evaporate in harsh midday heat.
2. Remove dried leaves, pull out wild weeds by hand, and add organic dry-leaf compost once every fortnight.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M proper watering schedule + 1.5M weeding and natural composting.

Unit 2: Birds & Kindness • Class 3 English (Classic CBSE)

Unit 2: Bird Talk & Nina and the Baby Sparrows

Poem on How Birds View Humans & Heartwarming Story of Nina Protecting Sparrow Chicks

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'Bird Talk': Robin and Jay talking in the garden about how strange humans are (no feathers, no beetles to eat, sitting on wires).
  • Story 'Nina and the Baby Sparrows': Nina's worry about baby sparrows trapped in her room during a family wedding.
  • Compassionate solution: Leaving the window wide open so mother and father sparrow can feed their babies.
  • Grammar: Describing words (adjectives: plump, tiny, worried, happy).
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What do Robin and Jay think of people in 'Bird Talk'? Why was Nina crying and refusing to buy new wedding clothes in the market? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Robin & Jay's Thoughts: Robin and Jay find human beings funny and strange because humans don't grow feathers, cannot fly, don't eat beetles, and cannot sit on wires and twigs.
2. Nina's Worry: Nina was crying because there was a sparrow's nest on her bookshelf with two tiny, featherless baby sparrows. If the house was locked for her aunt's wedding in Delhi, the mama and papa sparrows would not be able to enter to feed their hungry babies.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of Robin & Jay's view of humans 1.5 M
Nina's concern for trapped baby sparrows and closed room 1.5 M
Q2 What clever plan did Nina's mother suggest that solved Nina's problem and protected the baby sparrows? Problem Solving • Kindness to Animals 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Mother's Plan:
Mother suggested removing Nina's clothes and books from the room, locking the room door from the outside, but leaving the bedroom window wide open. This kept the house secure while allowing the parent sparrows to fly in and out freely to feed the chicks.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Mention of locking door from outside 1.5 M
Leaving window open for parent sparrows 1.5 M
Q3 Pick the suitable describing word from brackets: (a) A ___ (fat / thin) baby sparrow was flying happily. (b) Nina was very ___ (sad / angry) about the birds. (c) A ___ (beautiful / ugly) red dress was bought for the wedding. Grammar • Adjectives (Describing Words) 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answers:
• (a) Two plump / fat baby sparrows were flying happily.
• (b) Nina was very sad / worried about the birds.
• (c) A beautiful red dress was bought for the wedding.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct adjectives selected for all 3 blanks 3.0 M
Q4 In 'Nina and the Baby Sparrows':
(a) Why was everyone in Nina's family thrilled and getting ready to go to Delhi?
(b) Why was Nina sad and crying?
(c) What clever solution did Nina's mother find so that the baby sparrows would be safe? Reading is Fun • Nina and the Baby Sparrows 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Details:
(a) Family Joy:
• Nina's family was going to Delhi for her aunt's grand wedding.

(b) Nina's Worry:
• Nina was crying because there was a sparrow nest on her bedroom bookshelf with two tiny baby sparrows who were just growing their feathers. If the house was locked, mother and father sparrow could not come in to feed them.

(c) Mother's Solution:
• Mother said they would remove all things from the room, leave the bedroom window wide open, and lock the main door from outside so the mother and father sparrows could fly in and out freely.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct mention of aunt's wedding in Delhi 1.0 M
Sensitive empathy for feeding baby sparrows 1.0 M
Mother's open-window solution explained 1.0 M
Q5 In the poem 'Bird Talk':
(a) Name the two birds who sit in the garden and talk to each other.
(b) What three things do people not have or do, which the birds find so funny? Poem Comprehension • 'Bird Talk' 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poem Analysis:
(a) The Two Birds:
• Robin and Jay.

(b) What Birds Find Funny About People:
• 1. People don't grow feathers at all.
• 2. People don't eat beetles or insects.
• 3. People cannot sit on wires and tree branches like birds do.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct names: Robin and Jay 1.0 M
Three funny traits of humans from birds' perspective 2.0 M
Q6 Arrange the following sentences in correct chronological order of the story (1 to 4):
• Nina comes back from Delhi and finds two plump little sparrows flying in her room.
• Mother suggests leaving the window open.
• Nina's aunt is getting married in Delhi.
• Nina refuses to buy a new dress because she is worried about baby sparrows. Picture Sequencing • Story of Nina 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Chronological Sequence:
1. Nina's aunt is getting married in Delhi.
2. Nina refuses to buy a new dress because she is worried about baby sparrows.
3. Mother suggests leaving the window open.
4. Nina comes back from Delhi and finds two plump little sparrows flying in her room.

Correct order of all 4 key plot events 3.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Urban Bird Conservation

Real-Life Context: House sparrows were once common in every household balcony, but modern glass buildings and lack of grains have caused sparrow numbers to drop drastically.

Analytical Task: What two simple things can apartment residents do on their balconies to help house sparrows survive in cities?

1. Hang an earthen shallow water bowl (bird bath) and a small wooden birdhouse out of reach of predators.
2. Place small grains (millets, bajra, broken rice) on window sills daily for food.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M providing water bowl and safe nesting box + 1.5M providing grains daily.

Unit 3: Growth & Teamwork • Class 3 English (Classic CBSE)

Unit 3: Little by Little & The Enormous Turnip

Acorn Growing into an Oak Tree & Classic Folk Tale of Collective Strength

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'Little by Little': An acorn hidden in the earth slowly drinking dew, sending roots down and shoots up.
  • Gradual growth: How small efforts every single day lead to immense strength and majestic branches.
  • Story 'The Enormous Turnip': Old man, old woman, boy, and girl pulling together to harvest the giant turnip.
  • The moral of collective effort: 'United we stand, divided we fall'.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What does the acorn need to grow into a mighty oak tree? Who all helped in pulling up the enormous turnip? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Acorn's Growth: The acorn needs fertile soil to hide in, cool morning dew drops to drink, warm sunshine, and fresh air to grow roots downward and slender branches upward year by year.
2. Turnip Team: Four people pulled together: the old man, the old woman, the young boy, and the young girl.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Acorn's growth requirements (soil, dew, sunlight, time) 1.5 M
All 4 characters in the turnip pulling line identified 1.5 M
Q2 Could the old man pull out the turnip by himself? What lesson does this teach us about doing difficult tasks? Moral & Character Insight 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Moral Lesson:
• No, the old man could not pull out the giant turnip alone, nor could the old woman and boy alone.
• Lesson: When a task is too big for a single individual, coming together and working as a united team achieves victory easily. Cooperation and teamwork conquer difficulties.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct statement of old man's inability alone 1.0 M
Clear moral of unity, cooperation, and teamwork 2.0 M
Q3 Give the meaning of: (a) Slender, (b) Mighty, (c) Enormous. Use 'enormous' in a sentence. Vocabulary • Plant Growth Terms 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Word Meanings:
• (a) Slender: Thin, delicate, and graceful.
• (b) Mighty: Very strong, powerful, and grand.
• (c) Enormous: Extremely large in size or quantity.

Sentence: 'The elephant walked through the forest with an enormous branch in its trunk.'
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate definitions for all 3 words 1.5 M
Correct grammatical sentence with enormous 1.5 M

(c) Who finally helped to eat the delicious turnip? Reading is Fun • The Enormous Turnip 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Details:
(a) Planted:
• The old man planted turnip seeds.

(b) People who Pulled (in Order):
• 1. The old man
• 2. The old woman
• 3. The young boy
• 4. The young girl.

(c) Who Ate the Turnip:
• All four of them (the old man, the old woman, the boy, and the girl) cooked and ate the delicious enormous turnip together.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct identification of turnip seeds 1.0 M
Accurate order of the 4 characters pulling 1.0 M
Collaborative eating described 1.0 M
Q5 In the poem 'Little by Little':
(a) Which tiny seed is speaking in the poem?
(b) Where does its slender root grow, and where does its threadlike shoot spring?
(c) What does the tiny acorn grow up to be eventually? Poem Comprehension • 'Little by Little' 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poem Analysis:
(a) The Seed:
• An acorn (the seed of an oak tree).

(b) Growth Direction:
• The slender root grows downward deep into the dark earth.
• The tiny threadlike shoot springs upward high into the air and sunlight.

(c) Full-Grown Form:
• It grows into the mighty oak tree, the forest's pride with broad branching limbs.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct acorn seed identified 1.0 M
Downwards root and upwards shoot contrast 1.0 M
Mighty oak tree named 1.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

School Cleanliness Drive Teamwork

Real-Life Context: The playground was covered with heavy fallen tree branches after a severe storm. No single student could lift them.

Analytical Task: How can the students apply the principle of 'The Enormous Turnip' to clean their school playground safely?

1. Instead of trying to lift heavy branches individually, four to five students can lift each branch together under teacher supervision.
2. Working in coordinated teams makes heavy physical tasks light, safe, and quickly accomplished.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M collaborative lifting concept + 1.5M safety and efficiency benefits.

Unit 4: The Sea & Self-Worth • Class 3 English (Classic CBSE)

Unit 4: Sea Song & A Little Fish Story

Poem on Hearing Ocean in a Shell & Classic Story of a Small Fish Saved by His Size

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'Sea Song': Finding a curly seashell on the sand, taking it home, and hearing a soft song inside.
  • Story 'A Little Fish Story': A tiny fish unhappy with his small size wishing to be big like others.
  • The turning point: Getting caught in a fisherman's net, where all big fish are trapped, but the tiny fish slips through the mesh to freedom.
  • Moral: Be grateful and content with who you are; every attribute has its unique purpose.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 Where did the child find the seashell, and what surprise happened when he held it to his ear? Why was the little fish unhappy at the beginning of the story? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Sea Song: The child found a curly seashell lying cold on the sea sand. When his mother held it to his ear, a soft, sweet, clear song seemed to sing from inside the shell.
2. Little Fish's Unhappiness: The little fish was constantly complaining because he was very tiny compared to the huge fish in his school and felt that being small made him unimportant.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct shell discovery and song heard from inside 1.5 M
Little fish's complaint about his small size 1.5 M
Q2 What happened when the fishermen hauled their net out of the water? How did being small save the little fish's life? Turning Point & Moral Discovery 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Climax & Moral:
• When the fishermen pulled the great net into the boat, all the big fish flopped helplessly, trapped by the netting.
• Because the little fish was so small, he wriggled easily through the tiny gaps in the net's mesh and splashed back down into the cool, safe ocean.
• From that day on, he never wished to be a single bit bigger!
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Description of net hauling and big fish trapped 1.5 M
Little fish slipping through mesh gaps to safety 1.5 M
Q3 Fill in the blanks with suitable collective nouns: (A ___ of fish, A ___ of birds, A ___ of wolves, A ___ of cows). Vocabulary • Collective Nouns 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Collective Nouns:
• A school / shoal of fish
• A flock of birds
• A pack of wolves
• A herd of cows
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct collective nouns for all 4 groups 2.0 M

✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poem Analysis:
(a) Shell Location:
• The child found the curly shell lying on the sandy seashore.

(b) The Surprise:
• The child was surprised and amazed to hear a soft, sweet, clear song singing inside the shell.

• Found — Ground
• Ear — Clear (or Hand — Sand).

(a) Why was the little fish unhappy?
(b) What happened when a huge fishing net trapped the whole school of fish?
(c) Why did the little fish never complain about being small again? Reading is Fun • A Little Fish Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Details:
(a) Unhappiness:
• The little fish was unhappy because he was so tiny compared to all the grand, big fish in the sea.

(b) Net Trapping:
• A giant fishing net swept through the sea, trapping the school of big fish.

(c) Escape and Lesson:
• As the heavy net was being hauled out of the water, the little fish wriggled right through the tiny mesh holes and swam safely back into deep, cool water. He realized being small saved his life!
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Reason for unhappiness (small size) 1.0 M
Trapped in net event 1.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Embracing Individuality & Self-Acceptance

Real-Life Context: In a school play, Kabir was sad because he was shorter than his classmates and thought he would not get a good role.

Analytical Task: How can the teacher help Kabir understand that each person has unique strengths just like the little fish in the story?

1. The teacher can explain that being agile, light, or quick allows children to excel in unique roles such as a fast runner, dancer, or special story character.
2. Reminding students that outer appearance does not determine talent helps children build self-worth and genuine pride in who they are.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M recognizing diverse talents + 1.5M building healthy self-esteem.

Unit 5: Market & Kindness • Class 3 English (Classic CBSE)

Unit 5: The Balloon Man & The Yellow Butterfly

Poem on Colourful Market Balloons & Gentle Story of Freeing a Butterfly from a Spider's Web

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'The Balloon Man': A vendor standing in the market square with bunches of red, purple, blue, and green balloons.
  • Story 'The Yellow Butterfly': Sonu chasing a pretty yellow butterfly resting on a red rose, lotus leaf, and peach tree.
  • Rescuing from danger: The butterfly caught in a hungry black spider's web, and Sonu setting it free to flutter happily in the sky.
  • Vocabulary: Colour adjectives and gentle animal handling verbs.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 Where does the Balloon Man stand in the poem? Why did Sonu decide to let the yellow butterfly go in the end? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. The Balloon Man: The balloon man stands in the market square holding bunches of bright balloons tied with string on sunny and windy market days.
2. Sonu's Kindness: Sonu initially chased the butterfly to catch it. But when he saw it struggling helplessly in the spider's web, he realized how sad and frightened it looked in his hands. He wanted it to be happy, so he released it to fly freely from flower to flower.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct location of the balloon man in market square 1.0 M
Clear explanation of Sonu's empathy and decision to free it 2.0 M
Q2 Where did the butterfly rest before getting caught in the web? List the three places Sonu saw it land. Sequencing Events • Story Flow 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Sequence of Places:
1. First, on a red rose in the garden.
2. Second, floating on a floating lotus leaf in the pond.
3. Third, perched among the sweet pink peach blossoms on the peach tree.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct three resting spots in order 3.0 M
Q3 Write the opposites for: (a) Never, (b) Small, (c) High, (d) Catch. Grammar • Opposites 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Opposites:
• (a) Never × Always
• (b) Small × Big / Large
• (c) High × Low
• (d) Catch × Release / Drop.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct opposites for all 4 words 2.0 M
Q4 In 'The Yellow Butterfly':
(a) Where did Sonu first see the yellow butterfly?
(b) Where did the butterfly escape from Sonu (three places in the garden)?
(c) Why did Sonu catch the butterfly, and why did he finally let it go free? Reading is Fun • The Yellow Butterfly 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Details:
(a) First Sighting:
• Sonu first saw the yellow butterfly flying in his garden.

(b) Three Escape Spots:
• 1. On a red rose flower.
• 2. Floating on a white lotus leaf in the pond.
• 3. High up in a peach tree with pink flowers.

(c) Rescue & Release:
• The butterfly got trapped in a hungry spider's web. Sonu gently rescued it from the spider, held it in his hand, saw how sad it looked, and let it fly free because he wanted it to be happy.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Garden sighting 1.0 M
Three authentic locations (rose, lotus, peach tree) 1.0 M
Rescue from spider web and empathetic release 1.0 M

✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poem Analysis:

• The balloon man stands in the crowded market square.

(b) Holding Balloons:

• All living creatures have a right to live freely in nature. Caging birds or catching butterflies deprives them of their freedom, frightens them, and disrupts nature's ecological balance where butterflies help pollinate flowers.

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Wildlife Freedom vs Caging

Real-Life Context: Some people trap colourful wild birds like parrots in tiny cages to keep as pets in their living rooms.

Analytical Task: Based on the moral of 'The Yellow Butterfly', why is freedom better for wild creatures than life inside a cage?

1. Birds and butterflies are born with wings meant to fly in the open blue sky and live naturally in trees.
2. Confining them in cages causes misery and prevents them from living natural lives; true love for nature means admiring animals in freedom, not caging them.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M natural purpose of flight and habitat + 1.5M ethical argument against caging.

Unit 6: Travel & Community • Class 3 English (Classic CBSE)

Unit 6: Trains & The Story of the Road

James S. Tippett's Poem on Trains & The Morning Awakening of the Village Road

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'Trains': Over mountains, plains, and rivers carry passenger cars, mail, and precious freight day and night.
  • Story 'The Story of the Road': Early morning silence on the road, awakened by chirping sparrows, caw of crows, newspaper boy's cycle bell, and vegetable seller.
  • Anthropomorphic storytelling: The road wishing the noisy crow would realize it is already wide awake.
  • Transportation vocabulary: freight, passengers, mail, level crossing, bicycle bell.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What precious loads do the trains carry across the country in 'Trains'? Who are the first creatures and people to awaken the road in the morning? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Precious Cargo: Trains carry thousands of passengers, precious mail, letters, and essential freight across mountains, plains, and rivers without failing.
2. First to Awaken the Road: The birds (chirping sparrows and cawing crows), the newspaper boy ringing his bicycle bell ('Tring-a-ling!'), and the vegetable seller calling out fresh peas, cauliflowers, and potatoes.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct freight, mail, and passenger details 1.5 M
Correct list of early morning road characters 1.5 M
Q2 Why was the road annoyed with the crow in 'The Story of the Road'? Story Humour • The Annoyed Road 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
The crow kept cawing foolishly: 'Caw! Caw! Wake up! Wake up!'. The road was annoyed because it was already wide awake, seeing the newspaper boy, smelling the vegetables, and hearing school children chattering. The road thought: 'Can't you see, you silly bird? I am wide awake!'
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of crow's repetitive wake up call 1.0 M
Road's annoyance at already being wide awake 1.0 M

✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Sound Matching:
• 1. Bicycle bell → Tring-tring
• 2. Shoes of children → Tramp-tramp
• 3. Crow → Caw-caw
• 4. Sparrows → Chirp-chirp.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct matching for all 4 sound words 2.0 M

(a) Name three geographical places over which the trains travel.

(c) Do trains stop traveling at night or during dark hours? Poem Comprehension • 'Trains' 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poem Analysis:
(a) Geographical Places:
• Over the mountains, over the plains, and over the rivers.

(b) Cargo:
• They carry thousands of passengers and heavy freight / precious mail.

(c) Night Travel:
• No, trains rush on continuously through day and dark, through dawn and dusk without stopping.

Mountains, plains, rivers named 1.0 M
Passengers and precious mail noted 1.0 M
Continuous day-night travel described 1.0 M

(a) What sounds awaken the road early in the morning?
(b) Who is the first person to travel down the road in the morning?
(c) Why is the road annoyed with the crow? Reading is Fun • The Story of the Road 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Details:
(a) Morning Sounds:
• Birds chirping ('chirp-chirp'), crows cawing ('caw-caw'), newspaper boy's bicycle bell ringing ('trin-trin'), and vegetable man's cart.

(b) First Person:
• The newspaper boy on his bicycle, followed closely by the vegetable man.

(c) Road's Annoyance with Crow:
• The crow keeps shouting 'Caw, caw, wake up!' but the road is already wide awake and says, 'Foolish bird! Can't you see I am already wide awake!'
