🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Road Safety Rules for Children

Real-Life Context: Every morning, hundreds of students walk, cycle, or ride buses along busy city roads to reach school safely.

Analytical Task: State three golden road safety rules every primary school student must follow when walking to school.

1. Use the Footpath: Always walk on the designated pedestrian pavement or footpath.
2. Zebra Crossing: Cross the road only at marked zebra crossings or pedestrian footbridges.
3. Look Both Ways: Stop, look right, look left, and look right again before crossing, never running blindly across roads.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1M footpath rule + 1M zebra crossing + 1M look both ways rule.

Unit 7: Animals & Companionship • Class 3 English (Classic CBSE)

Unit 7: Puppy and I & Little Tiger, Big Tiger

A.A. Milne's Poem on Choosing a Playful Puppy & Story of a Tiger Cub Growing in the Wild

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'Puppy and I': Meeting a Man, Horse, and Puppy; choosing to go with the puppy who is going to roll and play.
  • Story 'Little Tiger, Big Tiger': Mother tigress and her cub living near a river in the shady jungle.
  • Hunting in the wild: Hunting for deer and wild boar; cub chasing a little leaping frog.
  • The roar of adulthood: The cub growing big and terrifying other jungle animals with his deep roar.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why did the child in 'Puppy and I' decide to go with the puppy instead of the man or horse? What happened when the little tiger cub chased a frog? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Choosing the Puppy: The man was going to the village to buy bread, and the horse was going for hay. But the puppy was going up in the hills to roll and play, which matched the child's playful spirit.
2. Chasing the Frog: The tiger cub chased a bouncing green frog far away from his mother in the dark jungle. When he caught the frog, he looked up and saw another giant tiger staring at him! Luckily, his mother tigress roared loudly, driving the stranger away.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct explanation of choosing the puppy for play 1.5 M
Details of chasing frog and encountering stranger tiger 1.5 M
Q2 Give the name of the home and young one for: (1) Tiger, (2) Horse, (3) Dog. Options: (Lair/Den, Stable, Kennel; Cub, Foal, Puppy). Animal Homes & Sounds 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Animal Facts:
• 1. Tiger: Home = Lair / Den | Young One = Cub
• 2. Horse: Home = Stable | Young One = Foal / Colt
• 3. Dog: Home = Kennel | Young One = Puppy.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct homes and young ones for all 3 animals (1M each) 3.0 M
Q3 The tiger is India's National Animal. Why are tigers endangered, and what is 'Project Tiger'? Wildlife Conservation Awareness 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Tiger Conservation:
1. Why Endangered: Tigers lost their forest habitats due to deforestation and were illegally hunted by poachers for their skins and bones.
2. Project Tiger: Launched by the Government of India in 1973, Project Tiger created protected National Parks and Tiger Reserves (like Jim Corbett and Ranthambore) to save tigers and restore healthy forest ecosystems.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Reasons for endangerment (poaching and habitat loss) 1.5 M
Explanation of Project Tiger and protected reserves 1.5 M

(c) What happened when the little tiger cub chased a frog deep into the jungle? Reading is Fun • Little Tiger, Big Tiger 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Details:
(a) Habitat:
• They lived in a shady jungle near a quiet river.

(b) Night Prey:
• She hunted deer and wild pigs.

(c) Chasing the Frog:
• The cub chased a tiny hopping frog far from his mother. When he caught it, he turned around and saw a huge, terrifying full-grown tiger staring at him! He was terrified until mother tiger arrived and let out a mighty roar that chased the stranger away.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Jungle habitat near river 1.0 M
Hunting deer and pigs 1.0 M
Encounter with big tiger and mother's protective roar 1.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Forest Food Chain Balance

Real-Life Context: Tigers are apex predators at the top of the forest food chain. If tigers disappear from a forest, the deer population multiplies out of control.

Analytical Task: How does the presence of tigers maintain the ecological balance of plants and water in a jungle?

1. By controlling the population of herbivores like deer and wild boar, tigers prevent overgrazing of forest grass and young tree saplings.
2. This keeps the forest canopy thick, protects topsoil from erosion, and ensures natural water springs continue flowing.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M herbivore population control + 1.5M protecting vegetation and soil balance.

Unit 8: What's in the Mailbox? & My Silly Sister

Poem on Receiving Letters & Rabindranath Tagore's Humorous Story on an Innocent Baby Sister

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'What's in the Mailbox?': Child watching postman bring letters for parents and deciding to write letters to friends so they write back.
  • Story 'My Silly Sister': An elder brother complaining affectionately to his mother about his baby sister's innocent antics.
  • Baby antics: Eating pebbles thinking they are real food, tearing book pages, laughing when scolded.
  • Affectionate sibling bonds: The loving warmth underlying playful sibling teasing.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What does the child plan to do in 'What's in the Mailbox?' so that letters arrive for him? What funny things does the baby sister do in Tagore's story? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Child's Plan: The child decides to write letters to his own friends so that they will write back and the postman will bring letters with his name on them.
2. Baby Sister's Antics:
• She thinks pebbles are real food and tries to put them in her mouth.
• When her brother opens a book to study, she tears the pages with joy.
• When her brother scolds her by shaking his head, she giggles thinking it is a fun game.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct child's strategy to write letters first 1.5 M
Two humorous baby antics described accurately 1.5 M
Q2 What four things must be written on an envelope to ensure a letter reaches the correct destination? Vocabulary • Letter Writing Terms 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Essential Envelope Details:
1. Recipient's Full Name: Name of the person receiving the letter.
2. House Number & Street: Exact residence location.
3. City / Village & State: Geographic town and province.
4. PIN Code (Postal Index Number): 6-digit postal code for accurate delivery.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
All 4 postal address elements identified 2.0 M

✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:

Please come to my 8th birthday party this Sunday, 15th October, at 5:00 PM at my home. We will play fun games, burst balloons, and eat delicious cake together. I look forward to seeing you!
Your friend,
Aarav.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Salutation and clear invitation details (date, time, place) 1.5 M
Correct closing and friendly sign-off 1.5 M

(a) What silly things does the baby sister do with pebbles and books?
(b) What does she do when the elder brother gets cross and shakes his head at her?
(c) When father is away, what does the baby sister do when the brother says 'Father'? Reading is Fun • My Silly Sister 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Details:
(a) Silly Antics:
• She thinks pebbles are real food and tries to put them in her mouth. When a book is opened, she tears the pages with her hands and roars with joy.

(b) Brother Getting Cross:
• Instead of being scared, she laughs joyfully and thinks it is great fun.

(c) Mentioning Father:
• She looks around quickly in excitement, thinking her father is near.

Pebbles and book page tearing described 1.0 M
Laughing at brother's scolding 1.0 M
Excitement at hearing father's name 1.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Digital Communication vs Traditional Post

Real-Life Context: Today, people send quick WhatsApp messages and emails, but receiving a handwritten postcard in the mailbox still feels magical.

Analytical Task: Why does a handwritten postcard from a grandparent create a deeper emotional connection than a short text message?

1. A handwritten postcard shows personal time, care, and effort: the sender chose the card, wrote carefully in their own handwriting, bought a stamp, and posted it.
2. It is a tangible keepsake that a child can touch, re-read, and cherish in an album for years.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M personal effort and tangible keepsake + 1.5M emotional permanence.

Unit 9: Courage & Family Devotion • Class 3 English (Classic CBSE)

Unit 9: Don't Tell & He is My Brother

Poem on Secret Potential of Childhood & Heartwarming Story of Meena Carrying Her Little Brother

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'Don't Tell': A child patient with adults who say he is too small, secretly knowing he is a giant inside waiting to show the world.
  • Story 'He is My Brother': Twelve-year-old Meena carrying her four-year-old brother who cannot walk up a holy hill path.
  • The traveller's question: 'Why are you carrying that heavy load, my child?'
  • Meena's unforgettable reply: 'He is not a load, he is my brother!'
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 What secret does the child keep inside in 'Don't Tell'? Where were the people in 'He is My Brother' going? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Child's Secret: Although adults say he is too small to do big things, the child secretly knows that inside him sleeps a powerful giant capable of doing wonderful deeds when the right time comes.
2. People's Destination: The people in the story were walking up a winding path through pine trees to visit a holy shrine on the mountain.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of child's secret giant potential 1.5 M
Destination as holy shrine on mountain 1.5 M
Q2 Why was Meena carrying her four-year-old brother on her back? Why did she smile when the man asked if she felt the load? Character & Emotion Analysis 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Why carried: Her little brother was four years old and was unable to walk due to physical disability.
2. Meena's Smile: She smiled in surprise because to her, he was her cherished brother whom she loved deeply. When you carry someone out of pure love, they never feel like a burden or 'load'.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Brother's inability to walk 1.5 M
Profound explanation that love transforms burden into joy 1.5 M
Q3 Add the prefix 'un-' to form opposites for: (a) Able, (b) Happy, (c) Kind, (d) Fair. Grammar • Opposites with 'Un-' prefix 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Opposites using 'un-':
• (a) Able → Unable
• (b) Happy → Unhappy
• (c) Kind → Unkind
• (d) Fair → Unfair
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct prefix usage for all 4 words 2.0 M
Q4 In 'He is My Brother':
(a) Where were the people going along the mountain path?
(b) Who was Meena carrying on her back, and why couldn't he walk by himself?
(c) What did Meena reply when a man asked why she was carrying such a heavy load? Reading is Fun • He is My Brother 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Details:
(a) Destination:
• The people were climbing a steep, pine-scented mountain path to visit a holy shrine (temple) at the hilltop.

(b) Meena's Brother:
• Meena was carrying her four-year-old little brother. He was unable to walk by himself because his legs were weak.

(c) Meena's Famous Reply:
• Meena looked at the man with wondering eyes and replied lovingly: 'Load? Of course not! He is not a load—he is my brother!'
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Holy shrine mountain path 1.0 M
Weak legs of 4-year-old brother 1.0 M
Iconic quote 'He is not a load, he is my brother' 1.0 M
Q5 In the poem 'Don't Tell':
(a) What do grown-ups always tell the child?
(b) What secret is the child hiding inside himself?
(c) When does the child say he will show everyone what he can do? Poem Comprehension • 'Don't Tell' 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poem Analysis:
(a) Grown-ups' Words:
• Grown-ups always tell the child, 'Wait till you are bigger! You are not old enough yet!'

(b) The Child's Secret:
• Inside himself, the child knows that he is really a giant in spirit and capability, with big dreams and courage.

(c) When He Will Show Everyone:
• He says he will show everyone when he grows up and gets his full chance.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Adults telling child to wait 1.0 M
Giant inside the child 1.0 M
Showing potential when grown up 1.0 M
Q6 Underline the silent letter in each of these words:
(a) Knife
(b) Comb
(c) Walk
(d) Listen Silent Letters • Pronunciation & Phonics 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Silent Letters:
• (a) Knife (Silent letter: k)
• (b) Comb (Silent letter: b)
• (c) Walk (Silent letter: l)
• (d) Listen (Silent letter: t)
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct silent letters identified for all 4 words 4.0 M
Q7 What valuable lesson about caring for our family members do we learn from Meena's love for her brother? Empathy & Family Love • Moral Value 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Moral Lesson:
• Meena teaches us that when we truly love our family and siblings, helping them is never a burden or a 'load'. Genuine love makes every sacrifice feel joyful, natural, and light.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Thoughtful reflection on unconditional sibling love 2.0 M
Q8 In 'Don't Tell & He is My Brother', describe what key lesson or character trait is highlighted when the central character faces a challenge. How does this connect to real-life friendship or cooperation? Reading is Fun • Direct Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Textual Comprehension & Analysis:
1. In the story/poem Don't Tell & He is My Brother, the central character demonstrates perseverance, kindness, and teamwork when confronting difficulties.
2. When individuals cooperate rather than act selfishly, problems are resolved much faster and everyone benefits.
3. Real-Life Connection: In our daily lives, sharing tasks with classmates or family members builds trust and mutual respect, just as seen in this lesson.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identification of central trait (cooperation/kindness) 1.5 M
Valid real-world connection to friendship/teamwork 1.5 M
Q9 From the lesson 'Don't Tell & He is My Brother', find:
(a) Two rhyming words or sound-alike pairs.
(b) Write the opposite (antonym) of: Kind, Fast, Heavy.
(c) Form a meaningful sentence using one of the new vocabulary words from this chapter. Word Building • Vocabulary & Phonics 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Vocabulary Solutions:
• (a) Rhyming pairs: Day - Play, Round - Sound.
• (b) Opposites:
- Kind → Cruel / Unkind
- Fast → Slow
- Heavy → Light.
• (c) Sample Sentence: The children showed great kindness by helping the injured bird.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct rhyming pairs 1.0 M
Accurate opposites for all 3 words 1.0 M

Q10 Have you ever had an experience similar to the events described in 'Don't Tell & He is My Brother'? Share what you did, who was with you, and how you felt afterward. Talk Time • Oral Expression & Personal Reflection 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Model Personal Reflection:
• Experience: Yes, during our school sports day, our relay team was trailing behind. Just like the theme in Don't Tell & He is My Brother, we encouraged each other and stayed calm.
• Action: In the final lap, our teammate ran with full determination, and we secured second place.
• Feeling: I felt proud and joyful because supporting each other brought us closer together.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear narration of personal experience 1.5 M
Expression of feelings and thematic alignment 1.5 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Inclusion & Support for Differently-Abled Peers

Real-Life Context: A classmate who uses a wheelchair needs assistance reaching the first-floor computer lab in a school without a lift ramp.

Analytical Task: How should students and school authorities work together to create an inclusive environment for differently-abled students?

1. Classmates can take turns carrying schoolbags and keeping them company with respect and cheerful companionship.
2. School authorities must install accessible ramps, grab rails, and hold ground-floor classes so every child can move independently with dignity.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M peer assistance and empathy + 1.5M institutional accessibility (ramps).

Unit 10: Animal Adaptations & Wonder • Class 3 English (Classic CBSE)

Unit 10: How Creatures Move & The Ship of the Desert

Poem on Animals' Natural Motion & Famous Dialogue Between the Camel and the Lion

Chapter Themes, Poetic Devices & Vocabulary Highlights
  • Poem 'How Creatures Move': Lion walks on padded paws, squirrel leaps, fly crawls, seals dive, worms wiggle, and boys/girls run and leap.
  • Story 'The Ship of the Desert': The Camel explaining his desert adaptations to the King of the Forest, the Lion.
  • Camel's survival tools: Thick padded feet that do not burn on hot desert sand, hump storing fat for weeks, and eating thorny bushes without hurting thick tongue.
  • Comparative dialogue and recognizing natural biological adaptations.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (20 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why is the camel called 'The Ship of the Desert'? How do the padded feet of the camel help it run across burning sand dunes? Reading is Fun • Poem & Story 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Answer:
1. Ship of the Desert: Just as a ship travels smoothly across ocean waters carrying people and cargo, the camel is the only animal that can travel tirelessly across vast sandy deserts without food or water for days.
2. Padded Feet: The camel has thick, wide, flat padded feet. The broad pads prevent its feet from sinking into loose sand, and the thick skin prevents the burning heat of the sand (over 200°F) from scorching its soles.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of Ship of the Desert metaphor 1.5 M
Scientific explanation of wide thick padded feet 1.5 M
Q2 What does the camel store in its hump, and what does it eat when there is no grass in the desert? Animal Adaptations • Biology in English 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Adaptation Facts:
• The Hump: The camel stores fat (stored food reserve) in its hump, which its body uses when food is unavailable.
• Desert Diet: It eats prickly thorns and desert bushes. Its mouth and tongue are so thick that sharp thorns cannot prick or hurt it.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct fact: stores fat (not liquid water) in hump 1.5 M
Thorny bushes and thick mouth explanation 1.5 M
Q3 Match each creature with its typical movement: (1) Lion, (2) Monkey, (3) Worm, (4) Bird. Movements: (Wiggles, Walks on padded paws, Swings by tail, Flies in air). Movement Words • Action Verbs 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Movement Matching:
• 1. Lion → Walks on padded paws
• 2. Monkey → Swings by tail
• 3. Worm → Wiggles
• 4. Bird → Flies in air.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct matching for all 4 animal motions 2.0 M
Q4 In 'The Ship of the Desert':
(a) Why is the camel called the 'Ship of the Desert'?
(b) How can a camel walk easily on burning desert sand where other animals cannot?
(c) Where does the camel store food and water, and for how many days can it survive without drinking? Reading is Fun • The Ship of the Desert 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Adaptation Science & Comprehension:
(a) Ship of the Desert:
• The camel is called the Ship of the Desert because it can navigate smoothly across endless oceans of burning desert sand dunes just like a ship sails across the sea.

(b) Walking on Hot Sand:
• Camels have broad, thick, padded feet that do not sink into loose sand, and the thick skin protects against scorching heat.

(c) Hump & Survival:
• The camel stores food as fat in its hump and can survive up to two weeks (14 days) without drinking water.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Origin of title 'Ship of the Desert' 1.0 M
Thick padded feet adaptation explained 1.0 M
Hump fat storage and 2 weeks survival fact 1.0 M
Q5 In the poem 'How Creatures Move':
(a) Match how each animal moves: Lion, Squirrel, Fly, Worm.
[Crawls, Walks on padded paws, Hops/Leaps, Creeps up a wall]
(b) How do boys and girls have much more fun than all these animals? Poem Comprehension • 'How Creatures Move' 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Poem Analysis:
(a) Animal Movements:
• Lion $\rightarrow$ Walks on padded paws
• Squirrel $\rightarrow$ Hops and leaps from limb to limb
• Fly $\rightarrow$ Creeps straight up a wall
• Worm $\rightarrow$ Wiggles all around / crawls.

(b) Boys and Girls:
• Boys and girls have much more fun because they can do all movements: they can leap, dance, walk, and run!
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Correct animal movement matches 1.5 M
Human versatility (leap, dance, walk, run) highlighted 1.5 M
Q6 Compare how animals adapt to their environments by filling in the table:
• Desert Animal (Camel): Features for heat and water scarcity.
• Forest Animal (Tiger): Features for hunting and camouflage. Desert vs Forest Animals • Comparison Table 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Adaptation Comparison Table:
Animal & HabitatKey Body AdaptationPurpose in Habitat
Camel (Desert)Padded feet, hump for fat storage, long eyelashesWalk on hot sand, survive without water, keep sand out of eyes
Tiger (Forest)Striped coat, sharp retractable claws, night visionCamouflage in tall grass, stealthy stalk and capture of prey
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Two accurate camel adaptations listed 1.5 M
Two accurate tiger adaptations listed 1.5 M
Q7 In the chapter dialogue, what does the lion say when the camel invites him to walk in the desert? Dialogue • Camel and Lion Conversation 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Story Dialogue:
• When the camel proudly offers to carry the lion across the desert sand, the lion looks down at his own paws, feels the blazing heat of the sand, and says respectfully: 'No, thank you! I'd rather stay right here in my cool green forest!'
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate recounting of lion's humorous refusal 2.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Animal Adaptations Across Biomes

Real-Life Context: While the camel thrives in hot Thar deserts, the Polar Bear thrives in freezing Arctic snow, and the Lion rules African grasslands.

Analytical Task: Why would a Lion struggle to survive in the Thar desert even though he is called the 'King of the Jungle'?

1. The Lion does not have wide padded feet to prevent sinking in loose sand, nor does he have thick soles to tolerate burning ground.
2. The Lion requires large quantities of water daily and abundant prey animals (zebras, deer), which do not exist across waterless desert dunes.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5M physical feet limitations in hot sand + 1.5M lack of water and prey in desert.
